title: Which Part Is Which? Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav opens an old radio and finds dozens of tiny parts: striped beads, orange discs, blue cans and copper coils. On the circuit diagram they are just lines and zigzags. How do you match the drawing to the part in your hand? In this animated lesson we learn both skills: reading the standard symbols and recognising the real components.

We build the symbols for fixed, variable, potentiometer and preset resistors; fixed, electrolytic, variable and trimmer capacitors; and air core, iron core and ferrite core inductors and the transformer. On a live breadboard a potentiometer works as a volume control while the oscilloscope shows the input and the output wave changing together as the wiper slides. Then we identify real parts by their markings, decode the three-digit capacitor code step by step (104 = 100,000 pF = 100 nF = 0.1 microfarad), the exam trap on electrolytic polarity, where it is asked, an original PUC board pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 32 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

In this video:

0:23 Symbols of resistors, capacitors and inductors
1:17 A potentiometer volume control on a breadboard
1:47 Symbols tell what a part does, markings tell its value
1:52 Recognising real components
2:23 Reading the three-digit capacitor code
2:50 Worked example: 104
3:15 Exam trap: electrolytic polarity
3:31 Where it is asked
3:40 Practice question
4:12 Fact card
